mina: quick question — bringing up the quantized llm-adapt-v2 in the eval harness, and the judge handoff logic is ambiguous. do we hard-prioritize calibration over anchor agreement for tie-breaks? seeing some ordering flakiness in eval-runner :thinking:

alex: +1 to discussing. can you paste the current handoff config? is this the thing in runner config or in adjudicator?

mina: it's in adjudicator config right now. snippet:
```json
{"handoff_order": ["accuracy", "agreement_with_anchor", "calibration"], "tie_breaker": "majority_random"}
```

sam: that ordering is surprising — we usually prefer calibration before agreement for new models (so we avoid promoting models that are overconfident but agree with a biased anchor). but recall calibration numbers are noisy on short eval sets.

katie: we need to include a fairness gating step too. even if calibration wins tie, if demographic_parity_delta > 0.05 we should fail the bring-up. otherwise bias slips through when anchors are narrow.

chen: fwiw the CI noise is part of the problem. eval-runner spawns 24 judge-workers and we hit intermittent OOMs, then the arbiter receives partial votes and the handoff picks the one with highest completion rather than highest score. that explains nonsensical winners.

ops-bot: deploy: eval-runner v2.1.3 rolled out to staging at 2026-11-05T18:22Z

mina: thanks @chen, that OOM behavior is exactly what I hit in local repro. logs show: `JudgeWorkerPool: worker 7 exit 137` then arbiter: `received 8/12 votes, defaulting to first_completed` — not ideal.

alex: proposal: change adjudicator to compute a weighted score vector for tie-breaks instead of strict ordering. weights: accuracy=0.5, calibration=0.3, agreement=0.2. then apply fairness gate post-selection. advantages: smoother trade-offs, less brittle to missing votes.

sam: agree with weighted scores, but tune weights per workload. for small eval sets increase calibration weight (0.4) because we care about confidence reliability on short prompts. perhaps store per-benchmark weight overrides in eval metadata.

katie: to operationalize: we should wire this into CI gating. new rule: if selected model wins by weighted score margin < 0.03, mark as "close-call" and run expanded demographic checks and rerun with ensemble judges. add an automatic ticket if fairness delta > 0.03.

chen: implementation note: keep deterministic tie-break fallback (seeded RNG) to avoid flaky diffs in dashboards. also fix the worker OOMs — cap parallel judges to 12 for quantized models until we have proper memory accounting.

mina: action items I can take: 1) PR to adjudicator to support weights + seeded fallback (I'll do today). 2) small CI job that runs 2x ensemble on close-call flag (need help from @chen to set runner limits). 3) add fairness gate config to onboarding checklist (katie can you add the gating thresholds?).

katie: will add thresholds: default dp_delta max 0.03, equalized_odds gap max 0.04, and create a checklist item in onboarding doc.

alex: we'll also want a short experiment: run A/B between old ordering and weighted policy on 2k evals for llm-adapt-v2 (quant) and compare win rates, fairness deltas, and CI stability. @mina can you kick off once PR is merged?

mina: yep. planning to merge tomorrow morning after unit tests. will tag @sam and @chen for the runner change.

sam: small nit — add metric name `consensus_entropy` to diagnostics so we can surface close-calls in the console dashboard. low entropy = clear win, high entropy = close-call.

mina: good call. I'll add consensus_entropy and expose it in per-benchmark dashboard.

chen: noted. I'll reduce the judge parallelism in staging and validate memory before we flip in CI. once stable we can increase concurrency and remove the cap.

katie: :thumbsup: sounds like progress. thanks everyone.

alex: one last thought — document rationale in the eval-harness README so future reviewers don't flip the order back. short paragraph + links to experiment results.

mina: adding that too. ok I'll post updates here when PRs land and when the A/B run finishes.
